name: AerCap Holdings NV
reason: Aircraft lessor with EPS at its 10y high (USD 15.37 vs 6.19 in 2015) on a tight aircraft-supply market and elevated gains on sale, financed at 6.8x net debt/EBITDA with 2.6% avg ROIC; consensus FY2 -4.1% so normalised lease rates and funding costs cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: NatWest Group Plc
reason: Fails the through-cycle bank test: 10y avg ROE 6.0%, EPS went nowhere in the zero-rate years (GBP 0.28 in 2015 to 0.25 in 2021, loss in 2020) and the 2025 high of 0.68 is peak-NIM driven.

name: Nova Ljubljanska banka d.d.
reason: EPS jumped from EUR 11.66 (2021) to 27.44 (2023) on the rate cycle and has since slipped to 24.77 with FY1 consensus +3%; Balkan expansion and a 25% Slovenian state stake make a non-NIM 7% route hard to underwrite despite 14.7% avg ROE.

name: Raiffeisen Bank International AG
reason: Russia/Belarus exposure set the record (EPS EUR 10.76 in 2022 to 3.19 in 2024, now 0.38x its 10y max) and 10y avg ROE is 10.7%; earnings depend on sanctions and geopolitics, not franchise strength.

name: Arion Banki hf
reason: Icelandic bank with no 10y EPS growth (ISK 20.98 in 2015 to 21.86 in 2025, 0.4% CAGR) and 10.1% avg ROE; recent recovery is rate-driven and growth comes from buybacks in a small concentrated market.

name: ZIGUP PLC
reason: Cyclical commercial-vehicle hire/claims business with 1.0% 10y EPS CAGR (GBP 0.48 to 0.53), 5.5% avg ROIC, shares +5.5%/yr from the Redde merger and a 31% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap; cheap but ordinary.

name: Vienna Insurance Group AG
reason: CEE insurance growth is real (EPS EUR 2.13 in 2016 to 6.46 in 2025) but 10y avg ROE is only 8.2%, the 2023+ step-up coincides with IFRS 17, and the pending Nürnberger acquisition plus mutual-holding control blur the organic 7% route.

name: Islandsbanki hf
reason: Recently privatised Icelandic bank with 8.5% avg ROE and EPS flat at ISK 12.3-13.6 since 2022 after a share consolidation; no evidence of best-in-class through-cycle returns.

name: BW Energy Ltd.
reason: Offshore oil E&P (Gabon, Brazil, Namibia) whose earnings are set by oil prices and field development, with NTM FCF yield -13.7% and FY2-FY3 consensus swings of +124%/+169%.

name: KGHM Polska Miedz S.A.
reason: State-controlled copper miner: earnings set by copper prices and Polish mining tax (EPS PLN -24.58 in 2015, 30.81 in 2021, -18.49 in 2023), 1.6% 10y EPS CAGR and 6.1% avg ROE.

name: OTP Bank Nyrt
reason: Best record in the batch (EPS HUF 729 in 2016 to 4,456 in 2025, 9/10 years >=7%, 18.1% avg ROE) but growth leans on serial CEE/CIS acquisitions, Russia/Ukraine exposure, Hungarian windfall taxes and rate caps, and a 16% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap, so 10y earnings cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: ageas SA/NV
reason: EPS rose EUR 3.52 to 8.80 over 10y with 10% avg ROE, but earnings depend on Asian JVs (China Taiping) and investment markets, and the transformational esure acquisition (acq-to-FCF 9.0x over 10y) clouds the organic route.

name: Dios Fastigheter AB
reason: Leveraged Swedish regional property owner (net debt/EBITDA 9.8x) with FFO/share flat at SEK 6.0-6.4 since 2023, EPS 0.33x its 10y max, shares +4%/yr; rate- and valuation-driven with no 7% route.

name: Frasers Group PLC
reason: Controlling-shareholder retail/stake-building conglomerate (Mike Ashley) with 3/10 years of >=7% EPS growth, 6.6% avg EBIT margin, negative LTM FCF and acquisition-led growth; governance and capital allocation are not forecastable.

name: Jet2 PLC
reason: Airline/package-holiday operator at peak EPS (GBP 2.08) with consensus FY1 -34.8% and LTG ~0%, exposed to fuel, FX and capacity cycles (2020-21 losses); net cash does not make airline economics forecastable.

name: PORR AG
reason: Construction contractor with reported EBIT margin around 0% (-0.3% latest, 1.0% 10y max), 4.6% avg ROIC and a 2020 loss; tender-driven low-margin work with no moat.

name: NN Group N.V.
reason: Dutch life/pension insurer with no 10y EPS growth (EUR 4.06 in 2015 to 4.17 in 2025), 6.2% avg ROE, a 48% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap and LTG ~4%; spread and market-driven earnings with no 7% route.

name: Mota-Engil SGPS SA
reason: Leveraged contractor (net debt/EBITDA 2.6x, 3.1% avg ROIC) with EBIT margin at a 10y high of 11.0% on African/Latin American mining and construction contracts, shares +4.1%/yr; cyclical peak with EM political risk.

name: TP ICAP Group plc
reason: Inter-dealer broker whose earnings follow capital-markets volumes: EPS GBP 0.28 to 0.32 over 10y (1.4% CAGR), shares +10.7%/yr, 4.6% avg ROE and a very large adjusted-vs-GAAP gap.

name: Metro Bank Holdings Plc
reason: Losses in 2019-2024 (EPS GBP -1.52 in 2020), negative avg ROE, 2023 rescue recapitalisation and shares +23.8%/yr; the balance sheet failed a stress test.
